headline: A Seoul Economic Daily explainer says no country can control all of AI by itself, and industry panelists argue that AI sovereignty means openness to collaboration.
score_reason: Explainer built on a July panel and a Stanford report; the Huang view dates from 2023; lowered by 2.
importance_line: It matters to governments in South Korea and Europe that want homegrown AI and to chip and cloud suppliers that sell it, but it offers no new decision or event.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports, in an explainer translated from Korean, that no country has built a complete AI stack of chips, memory, data centres, models and power, so "sovereign AI" (a country's control over its own AI) is hard to achieve alone. Industry panelists at AMD's July event said sovereignty is not isolation, and Stanford researchers concluded the core of the idea is calibrating interdependence rather than removing dependence, while Nvidia chief Jensen Huang has argued since 2023 that every country should build its own AI system.
notes: Article was AI-translated from Korean (quotes may not match originals) and draws on the AMD Advancing AI 2026 panel in San Francisco (22-23 Jul 2026) and a July Stanford HAI report. Huang's headline view is from Paris, Nov 2023 per the text.
